approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from real observations. It breeds from score-ranked groups of a greedy survivor population, uses its existing fragment crossover and local graph edits to build a fresh pool, and rejects invalid or previously evaluated identities. Its direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange route is disabled. Before each batch it fits a Gaussian process to the complete accepted archive using count fingerprints and a count-sensitive Tanimoto covariance. It draws correlated score functions over the pool and evaluates one still-available maximizer from each function. Real feedback then updates the archive, predictor, survivors and future breeders.
approach.novelty: Reserve only the final successful batch choice for the molecule with the greatest posterior variance remaining after accounting for the locations of the preceding choices and the inherited observation noise. Every preceding Thompson choice uses exactly the original draw and mask. This tests whether one deliberately information-seeking evaluation supplies useful later feedback. Earlier siblings removed sampled residuals or their correlation, froze later model learning, or optimized sampled immediate batch improvement; none establishes the value of this final variance choice. The older all-position conditioning experiment changed later random functions by assuming pending scores equaled their means. This proposal changes one acquisition objective, without assigning any score to a pending molecule.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior being tested is that every successful allocation position in n-62daf219c70a maximizes a sampled immediate score; no position deliberately collects a label that remains uncertain given the other pending evaluation locations. This is a candidate explanation for limited productive exploration, not an established causal diagnosis or a claim that model variance is calibrated. The actual three Parent summary.json and run.log files are complete and successful, with macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747; median_2 mean is 0.2244176914540413 with SD 0.0021281171113449416. The indexed Parent audit reports 629 best-generating-parent wins among 4350 accepted offspring, 258 sequential incumbent improvements and 2401 accepted offspring later used for breeding, so real learning and local progress already occur. The same-Parent initial-only GP control n-7de8feaf821f changes every later selected set and loses 0.15185627363148665 in the complete paired macro mean: ongoing accepted-label conditioning has a useful scoped contribution, jointly with its updating normalization. Mean-only allocation n-299096e31fe7 loses 0.07686116167690966, and independent allocation residuals n-54adc6a641e8 lose 0.018447481386582327, motivating preservation of the useful preceding correlated Thompson choices. Conversely, n-8a62df15e51f raises sampled incumbent-improvement utility but loses 0.05627557001043134; fourteen of its 669 zero-gain choices actually beat the frozen incumbent. Thus sampled immediate utility can miss real wins, but this does not prove variance-seeking is better. The specific older n-521f362b3777 mean-fantasy conditioning test changed 287 of 435 sets and reduced mean modeled batch correlation while losing 0.0018442146149799665 relative to its own exchange-containing Parent. Its locations, noiseless residual projection, whole-batch intervention and Parent/profile boundaries remain separate from this one-slot hypothesis.
hypothesis: Replace only the final successful posterior-selection position by the smallest-index maximizer of the original latent posterior variance conditional on earlier selected locations with the inherited observation noise, while preserving every preceding masked correlated Thompson choice and learning only from real accepted feedback.

finding_summary.headline: Variance-seeking labels changed predictions but never bred, and mean final score fell by 0.02279
finding_summary.insights: The missing benefit cannot be explained by a failure to select different molecules, accept their labels or update the predictor. This rule repeatedly spent its final evaluation on small, weak-scoring structures: 340 of 435 final choices had at most five heavy atoms, versus 18 in the Parent’s final positions. This accounts for most of the molecular assessment’s increase from 123 to 382 tiny accepted proposals overall. The winner’s mean variance fell only from 0.8596 before location conditioning to 0.8581 afterward, and conditioning changed the marginal-variance winner in just five batches. Thus the experiment mostly exposed uncertain molecules far from the selected prefix, rather than demonstrating a benefit from correcting within-batch redundancy. Their labels did provide measurable predictive information in the limited sense of fixed-history sensitivity and slightly lower observed next-query error; the omission contrast also changes normalization, and it does not establish calibrated uncertainty, information gain or endpoint mediation. Those modest predictive effects did not offset the unsuccessful final evaluations under this budget. The broader output still contains useful aromatic and heterocyclic families alongside reactive bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry; these chemical observations do not identify the cause of the endpoint loss. The negative contribution finding is conditional on this one-position rule, Parent composition and Search panel. It neither refutes ordinary accepted-label learning nor isolates the value of the covariance-conditioning term, and the registered complete exposed failure ends this rule without tuning its reserved count or schedule.
finding_summary.results: All 435 batches preserved the nine preceding Thompson choices on the same decision state. The final choice changed in 433 batches, always with a strict increase in remaining model variance; the other two choices coincided. Every final molecule was accepted. All 418 changed labels with a later fit opportunity altered next-batch predictions when compared with a passive fit omitting that row. Their next-query mean squared error fell slightly, from 0.0094934 with the row omitted to 0.0094283 with it included, although 89 of 418 next-batch comparisons worsened. None of the 435 final molecules beat its generating parent, improved the incumbent or was subsequently used for breeding. The Parent’s final positions produced 46 parent-beating molecules and 232 later-used breeders. Across the complete matched panel, mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.572880, a paired change of −0.022790 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were −0.045797, +0.011083 and −0.033656; 11 of 15 task/seed endpoints declined. Selection and later learning are confirmed; useful reserved-identity breeding and the performance prediction are not.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and heterocyclic families coexist with tiny fragments, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds and difficult ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-062b351ccb52 produces substituted indole/azaindole amides, linked nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-alkyl and cyclic amines, quinoline-linked nitrogen-carbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl frameworks. All supplied Child and accepted published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectory paths were present and read: each task has 900 observations across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, including 870 accepted optimizer proposals. No task is omitted and no comparison path is missing. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. The present comparison is therefore a complete matched chemistry comparison under the supplied Research in Depth profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task. The published n-62daf219c70a report records exact reproduction of its same-code source n-c55c3d520a2c; its own historical profile mismatch is not a missing pairing for this Child. The original gaps below retain that source history, rather than treating the baseline reproduction as an independent chemical discovery. Digest ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9 to 0.9138 and aromatic-string incidence 0.8552 to 0.8977. These are molecule-level incidences of SMILES text features, not fractions of atoms or perceived ring counts. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 on every task. A read-only CPU RDKit pass over the supplied trajectories supplies the explicitly labelled heavy-atom, bond and ring readings below; all accepted optimizer records parsed. Perceived cycles follow a graph ring-perception convention, not independent ring systems or proof of accessible three-dimensional geometry. The global aromatic abundance does not describe every leader: the leading seed-0 fluorinated imino/carbonyl molecule has no perceived aromatic atoms. Neutral strings also do not imply an absence of basic amines, and absent stereomarkers do not imply an absence of potentially stereogenic centres. The Child contains 382 accepted optimizer proposals with at most five heavy atoms, versus 123 in the Parent, with the Child count higher in every matched seed/task pair. These counts describe evaluated outputs; they do not identify which generator or acquisition component caused them. Rich ring chemistry coexists with N-halogen, O-halogen, peroxide and unconventional sulfur environments, strained-looking ring closures, and unspecified stereochemistry. Ordinary aryl fluorides, amines, amides and heterocycles also occur, so synthetic plausibility is questionable rather than uniformly impossible. Structural diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds, with much narrower families among nearby high-scoring records. Perceived graph differences, SMILES uniqueness and ring presence are not founder ancestry: no founder count, independent lineage count, component attribution or causal diversity benefit is inferred here. Scores quoted below are observed trajectory values, not new scores or measurements of synthesis, stability or biological activity. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not each seed's retained best molecule. Reproducible descriptor observations and source hashes are in .slots/L01-resume-20260928/r21-slot1-molecular/chemistry_observations.json; this audit path is documentation, not authority for SMILES citations. Citations come only from the digest and request-granted Child trajectories. Parent comparisons use the published paths granted by focus.artifacts.parent_trajectories; original gap reports were read through context.evidence_index.

per_task.generated_character: All three seed leaders have 24 heavy atoms by RDKit. Seed 0 evaluation 259 is an ethyl/dimethyl azaindole carrying an N-fluoro aryl amide and carbon-bound aryl chlorine. Seed 1 evaluation 252 retains an indole-like aryl-amide arrangement with methoxy substitution and a methylene bridge across its aromatic region; its perceived cycles include a four-membered cycle, so it should not be read as an ordinary unbridged indole. Seed 2 evaluation 236 is a vinyl/methyl/methoxy indole linked by an N-bromo amide to pyridine. The seed-1 sulfur-containing fused-aromatic amide at evaluation 195 and the N-H amide at evaluation 155 are real alternatives within the output; N-halogen substitution is not universal. The recognizable aromatic amide chemistry nevertheless has questionable local reactivity or ring geometry in its leading forms. Digest ring/aromatic-string incidences are 0.9/0.8851, halogen incidence 0.8218 and mean SMILES length 38.9. The accepted at-most-five-heavy-atom counts in Child/Parent seed order are 29/10, 26/8 and 29/8; larger molecules remain the dominant evaluated output.
liabilities: The three seed leaders contain N-F or N-Br on an amide nitrogen, chemically distinct from ordinary carbon-bound aryl halogens; their scores do not establish storage or synthetic stability.
The seed-1 methylene bridge constrains an aromatic region through a small perceived cycle. A valid aromatic SMILES is not a conformational assessment.
The output continues to include isolated heteroatom-halogen species and small peroxide or ether fragments at very low scores; retaining only these local groups loses the useful molecular context.
missing_features: Consistently conventional, stable nitrogen substitution preserving the successful aromatic/carbonyl relationships is not demonstrated at the leading scores; ordinary N-H amides are already present, so this is not a missing ability to make an amide.

The bridged aromatic leader lacks demonstrated geometric feasibility. Independent, plausible compact alternatives to the locally favored ring organization are not reliably established by the leading examples.
The observed gradient identifies no exact absent pharmacophore and does not justify adding rings, donors or halogens indiscriminately.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source: n-c55c3d520a2c molecular gap on heteroatom/benzylic halogen environments, reproduced in the same-code n-62daf219c70a baseline. Re-observed here in n-062b351ccb52 under the complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch size 10, 300 observations per task. Current leaders include N-fluoro or N-bromo amides, N-fluorinated imino/carbonyl rings, aryl O-Cl, O-F and nitroso groups; nearby records contain peroxides, and another seed leader has unconventional multiply bonded sulfur. Counterexamples matter: the linked azaaryl/nitrile leader and all leading aryl-amine examples have no N-halogen, O-halogen or peroxide bond. The historical fluorinated leader without N-F remains an additional boundary. This is environment-specific missing consistency, not inability to make amines, ordinary halogenated carbons or heterocycles.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments around otherwise useful aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs bond-environment-aware transformations and conventional local alternatives that preserve favorable structural relationships learned from its own accepted feedback. Keep ordinary carbon-bound halogens and useful nitrogen functions distinguishable from reactive heteroatom-halogen or unconventional sulfur environments. These observed associations do not establish that any universal filter improves score, and the original baseline reproduction and current panel do not attribute the liability to a specific retained component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source: n-c55c3d520a2c ring-geometry gap, reproduced in n-62daf219c70a; present evidence comes from n-062b351ccb52 on the matched Search panel at 300 observations per task and batch size 10. Current high-scoring structures include small methylene bridges across aromatic regions, a fused aromatic region with a perceived three-membered cycle, medium-ring nitrogen-carbonyl bridges, and cumulated unsaturation in a sulfur-containing ring. The historical small cyclic cumulene and large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring belong to the source nodes, not to every current leader. Noncumulated current fluorinated relatives and ordinary azaaryl/amine arrangements also score well. The current digest cumulated-double-bond-string rates are low, so this is a consequential local liability rather than a claim that most outputs are cumulenes.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish representable ring connectivity from geometrically credible unsaturation and bridge topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction needs ring-size, unsaturation and bridge-geometry awareness, with alternative plausible connectivities preserving learned functional arrangements. Perceived cycles and aromatic labels cannot supply conformational feasibility. Distinguish ordinary small or fused rings from unsupported bond geometry; neither a blanket ring ban nor a causal endpoint benefit follows from this chemistry assessment.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source: n-c55c3d520a2c stereochemical-identity gap, reproduced in n-62daf219c70a and re-observed in n-062b351ccb52 under the supplied matched Search Seeds and frozen budget/profile. Every current task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, while parsed leading aryl-amines, the alkylamino-linked heteroaromatic structure, fluorinated rings and bridged lactams contain unassigned potential centres. This does not apply to every structure: the compact aromatic amide leaders and a nitrogen-dicarbonyl leader have no perceived tetrahedral stereocentre. Formal-charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but clearly protonatable aliphatic amines are present.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output leaves potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres without specified stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and graph transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemical identity when the resulting chemistry requires it, while recognizing achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Assess protonation and tautomerism separately. The source and current observations establish unspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty, an obligation to enumerate every state, or attribution to one component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source: n-c55c3d520a2c context-loss/elaboration gap, reproduced in n-62daf219c70a. The current n-062b351ccb52 matched Search panel re-observes it under batch size 10 and 300 observations per task: at-most-five-heavy-atom accepted proposals total 382 versus 123 in the Parent, with a higher Child count in every seed/task pair. Tiny halogen, hydrocarbon, peroxide and heteroatom fragments often reach floor or very low scores, including final evaluations, while larger leaders combine several functional regions. Conversely, one seed grows a 67-heavy-atom leader below its much smaller published Parent counterpart. Useful simplification remains possible: deleting a thiol preserves a high aryl-amine score, nearby shortened linker variants retain similar values, and peripheral substitutions can tie. Size alone is not the capability gap.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful molecular context while avoiding excessive fragmentation and elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback can inform preservation, simplification or replacement of chemically useful relationships, so exploratory structures retain interpretable molecular context instead of repeatedly becoming trivial fragments or redundant appendages. The evidence does not authorize a universal molecular-size cutoff, a preference for larger molecules, or task-specific allocation. These are accepted-output associations; no fragmentation cause, acquisition activation, omitted-candidate score or component contribution is inferred.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source: n-c55c3d520a2c leading-family coverage gap, reproduced in n-62daf219c70a; current support is conditional on n-062b351ccb52 Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 and the same supplied evaluation budget/profile. Nearby high-scoring records repeatedly alter peripheral substituents, linker lengths, nitrogen environments or ring segments within recognizable families. The current seeds nevertheless reach markedly different compact, extended and bridged organizations, including an N-halogen-free azaaryl/nitrile leader and noncumulated fluorinated alternatives. Thus the output is not globally collapsed and can form new topology; what remains unestablished is reliable useful coverage of plausible alternative frameworks within a search. No number of founders, disjoint ancestry groups or independent discoveries has been inferred from perceived rings or SMILES differences.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not establish consistent coverage of chemically credible alternatives to its locally successful scaffold family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic scaffold transformations can offer chemically credible connectivities that retain favorable functional-group relationships learned locally. Assess those alternatives through their actual accepted feedback and chemistry, preserving adverse and seed-specific outcomes. Distinct strings or structural core counts alone do not establish independent ancestry, productive diversity, component attribution or a guaranteed objective improvement.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
